final_report.summary: Successfully implemented a Widget Visibility Dropdown menu in the AtlasForge Dashboard toolbar. The dropdown features checkboxes for all 17 dashboard widgets, allowing users to show/hide any widget without affecting backend WebSocket subscriptions or data collection. The implementation follows the existing toolbar UI patterns (modeled after the preset dropdown), uses localStorage for persistence across sessions, and includes bulk Show All / Hide All actions. Zero backend changes were required — hidden widgets simply get display:none applied while remaining in the DOM. All 17 tests passed including 5 adversarial edge-case tests (corrupt localStorage, non-existent IDs, rapid toggling, XSS vectors, double-open). The feature was verified visually via screenshots on display :99.
key_achievements: Added 'Widgets' dropdown button to toolbar with arrow indicator and dark-theme styling
Built checkbox-based multi-select dropdown that stays open during selection (unlike single-select preset dropdown)
Implemented WIDGET_REGISTRY mapping all 17 dashboard cards to human-readable labels
Added localStorage persistence so visibility preferences survive page refreshes
Included Show All / Hide All bulk action buttons for convenience
Exposed full public API (toggleWidgetVisDropdown, setWidgetVisible, isWidgetVisible, getHiddenWidgets, etc.) on window for programmatic control
Passed all 17 tests including 5 adversarial tests (corrupt storage, XSS, rapid toggle, missing elements)
Zero backend modifications — widgets stay in DOM with display:none, keeping WebSocket subscriptions active
Responsive design: label text hides on mobile (max-width 768px), keeping only the arrow
challenges_overcome: Ensuring dropdown stays open during multi-select while still closing on outside click — solved with stopPropagation on checkbox events
Matching existing toolbar visual patterns (preset dropdown) while implementing different interaction behavior (multi-select vs single-select)
Handling graceful degradation for corrupt localStorage data (returns empty array, defaults to all visible)
Registry synchronization — ensuring all 17 DOM card IDs matched the WIDGET_REGISTRY entries
lessons_learned: Reusing existing CSS patterns (.preset-dropdown) dramatically speeds up implementation and ensures visual consistency
Storing exceptions (hidden IDs) rather than full state means the default is always 'show everything' — safer and simpler
DOM display:none is the cleanest way to hide UI elements while keeping backend processes running — no need for complex conditional rendering
Adversarial testing (corrupt data, rapid toggling, XSS) catches edge cases that happy-path testing misses
Building the feature entirely client-side (JS + CSS + localStorage) avoided any dashboard_v2.py backend changes, reducing risk
